title: Update an abandoned old PC game for modern graphics
summary: A gamer had Claude Code with Opus 5.5 move The Movies (2005) to DirectX 11 and add visual upgrades without source code; they say it worked.
agent_role: The agent did the technical work of moving the game to a newer graphics system and adding visual improvements. The human supplied a bought copy of the game and the request.
outcome: The author reports the agent moved the game to DirectX 11 and added visual enhancements, and shares a video.
what_they_did: The poster owned a bought copy of The Movies (2005), a game its publisher abandoned. There was no source code. They asked Claude Code, running Opus 5.5, to move the game to DirectX 11, a newer graphics system, and to add visual upgrades.
how_it_went: The author says the agent did it and shares a video of the remastered game.
worth_knowing: The agent worked from the finished game files alone, with no original source code to read.
prompt: I own a legal copy of [game name], an old PC game installed at [install folder]. There is no source code. Study how the game draws its graphics and propose a plan to move it to [modern graphics system, e.g. DirectX 11] with visual improvements like [higher resolution, better lighting]. Work on a copy of the files, never the originals. Show me your plan before making changes, and test each step by launching the game.

curation.rationale: An unusual use: reviving an abandoned 2005 game without its source code, backed by a video. The post gives very few details about the steps.
